title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Maya Rodriguez
summary: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is the canonical reference for employees, team leads, and auditors.
purpose: Provide a single, actionable source of truth for common operational policies so teams can operate consistently, comply with security and financial controls, and avoid ad-hoc exceptions.
scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with company systems, data, procurement processes, or travel on behalf of Redwood. Exceptions must be documented and approved by the relevant owner_team and Security/Finance where required.
roles_and_responsibilities:
- People Ops: maintain and publish policies, manage role templates and onboarding/offboarding process.
- Security: approve access classifications, run periodic access reviews, and maintain RBAC standards.
- Finance: own procurement thresholds, approvals, and expense reimbursement rules.
- IT/Platform: implement technical access controls (Okta, IAM roles, Vault) and change management controls.
- Team Managers: validate access requests, approve procurement/expenses within delegated limits, and enforce data retention requirements.
access_and_permissions:
Policy summary:
- Principle: least privilege. Access is granted for a defined purpose and time-bound when possible.
- Identity providers: Okta is the authoritative identity provider for Redwood. All employees must authenticate through SSO and MFA.
- Role-based access: Standard roles (engineer, infra-admin, security-analyst, finance-reader) are defined in the Access Catalog. Managers must request non-standard access via the Access Request workflow.
- Privileged access (admin/root): requires sponsor approval + Security review; duration must be time-limited and logged.
- Access request workflow:
  1) Open an Access Request (Jira Service Desk ticket) with justification, expiry date, and approver.
  2) Manager approves (owner_team).
  3) Security reviews for privileged scopes.
  4) IT implements access and records in the Access Log.
  5) Automated reminders for expiry at 7 and 2 days prior.
- Periodic review: Quarterly access review led by Security; team managers must certify active access.
- Emergency access: Temporary emergency access is permitted via the Break Glass process; incidents are logged and reviewed by Security within 48 hours.
- Third-party/Vendor access: Must use least-privilege service accounts or short-lived credentials; vendor access approvals require vendor-management sign-off and contract clause for data handling.
change_management:
Policy summary:
- All changes to production systems follow the Change Management process. Changes are categorized: low-risk (routine), medium-risk (scheduled config), high-risk (schema, infra changes), and emergency.
- Change classification and approval matrix:
  - Low-risk: may be performed with dev-owner notification during business hours.
  - Medium-risk (>15 minute user impact potential): requires change ticket, test plan, and 24-hour planned window.
  - High-risk (>1 hour impact or data migration): requires CAB approval (includes engineering leads, SRE, Security, Product, and Finance if cost-impacting). Document rollback plan and runbook.
  - Emergency: use Emergency Change channel and follow emergency CAB post-facto review within 48 hours.
- Deployment practices: Canary followed by progressive rollout. Feature flags should be used where possible.
- Testing and sign-off: All non-trivial changes must include pre-deployment validation steps, post-deployment checks, and owner sign-off.
- Communication: Changes affecting customers or internal SLAs must be announced on Slack #platform-updates and the weekly change digest.
- Auditing: All change tickets must include link to PR, test evidence, and affected services. Records retained for 3 years.
data_management:
Policy summary:
- Data classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (PII/PHI). Owners must label datasets and storage locations.
- Data handling requirements:
  - Public: allowed in marketing/public repos. No restrictions.
  - Internal: default for internal metrics and product telemetry. Do not share externally without approval.
  - Confidential: requires encryption at rest and in transit (TLS + KMS-managed keys). Access restricted to role/need.
  - Regulated: additional contractual and technical controls (VPC-only, no backups outside region, stronger key management, audit logging). Consult Security before storing regulated data.
- Retention and deletion: Owners define retention periods in the Data Retention Catalog. Default retention for Internal logs = 90 days, Confidential = 1 year, Regulated = per-contract. Deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Request form and are executed by Data Stewards.
- Backups and DR: Backups must be encrypted and tested quarterly. Restore drills must be executed annually.
- Data provenance and cataloging: All production datasets must be registered in the Data Catalog with schema, owner, lineage, and sensitivity label.
- Data access checklist for onboarding datasets: purpose statement, retention, owner, approved access list, encryption, and monitoring hooks.
- Incident handling: Suspected data exposure triggers the Incident Response runbook and immediate notification to Security and Legal.
- Privacy & compliance: Work with Legal on DSARs, data transfer agreements, and vendor-data flow mapping.
procurement_and_expenses:
Policy summary:
- Purchasing thresholds and approvals:
  - <$1,000: team card purchase; manager approval required post-purchase for reconciliation.
  - $1,000-$25,000: Purchase Request (Coupa/Jira) with manager approval and Finance review.
  - >$25,000: Requires Finance + Legal review and Exec sponsor; attach SOW, SLA, and security questionnaire.
- Corporate card use: Cardholders must follow the Cardholder Guide. Personal expenses are not reimbursable. Lost/stolen cards must be reported to Finance immediately.
- Expense reimbursement: Submit receipts in the Expenses system within 30 days. Per diem and travel allowances follow the Travel Policy below.
- Contracting and commitments: Only authorized signatories may enter into contractual commitments. Non-standard terms require Legal approval.
- Budget ownership: Managers are responsible for staying within team budgets and approving expenses. Quarterly forecasting required for any recurring contract >$5,000/month.
- Record retention: Procurement records and contracts kept for at least 7 years as per Finance policy.
vendor_management:
Policy summary:
- Vendor selection: Teams must complete the Vendor Request Form and provide justification, estimated spend, and data access requirements.
- Security & compliance assessment:
  - Low-risk vendors: basic due diligence and security checklist.
  - High-risk vendors (access to Confidential/Regulated data): full security questionnaire, SOC 2 or equivalent evidence, penetration test summary, and contractual security SLA. Legal and Security must approve before onboarding.
- Contract requirements: Include data protection clauses, termination rights, audit rights, and breach notification timelines. Escalate to Legal for custom terms.
- Onboarding checklist: Legal sign-off, Finance purchase order, Security configuration (least-privilege accounts), and an onboarding runbook including contact matrix.
- Continuous monitoring: Annual vendor re-assessment and periodic access reviews. Remove stale accounts within 30 days of contract termination.
- Vendor incident response: Vendors must notify Redwood within 24 hours of any security incident affecting Redwood data. Coordinate through Security and Vendor Management.
- Offboarding: Revoke credentials, remove network access, and confirm secure disposal of Redwood data per contract terms.
travel_policy:
Policy summary:
- Booking and approvals: All business travel must be pre-approved via the Travel Request form. Managers approve travel; Finance reviews for budget compliance for trips >$5,000.
- Preferred vendors: Use approved travel vendors (Concur/TravelDesk) for bookings to ensure corporate rates and travel insurance.
- Expenses and per-diems: Submit itemized receipts. Per-diem rates follow the Finance schedule; otherwise actuals reimbursed up to reasonable policy limits. Alcohol is reimbursable only when part of a business meal and must be reasonable.
- Safety and duty of care: Register international travel with People Ops. Redwood provides emergency assistance contact and requires health insurance confirmation for extended trips.
- Reimbursement timeline: Submit expenses within 30 days; Finance processes reimbursements within 14 days from approval.
- Non-reimbursable items: personal entertainment, upgrades (unless pre-approved), and fines (e.g., traffic tickets).
- Travel for contractors: Contractors require a statement of work and pre-approval; contractors follow the same expense rules for reimbursable items.
templates:
This section points to standard internal templates to be used with the policies above. Use the canonical template stored in the Templates library. Examples:
- Access Request template: Templates/access-request-form.md
- Change Request & CAB template: Templates/change-request.md
- Vendor Risk Assessment checklist: Templates/vendor-risk-checklist.md
- Procurement Request form: Templates/procurement-request.md
- Travel Request form: Templates/travel-request.md
- Data Retention declaration: Templates/data-retention-declaration.md
- Offboarding checklist: Templates/offboarding-checklist.md
Note: Template names are case-sensitive in the Templates library and should be used as-is in requests and tickets.
